- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 period moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or bullish; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model often misjudges reversal timing; delay forecast drop by 1–2 periods unless sentiment confirms bearish momentum.
